///
///     override init(context: Context): bool {
///         this.source = context.audio("myAudio");
///         return true;
///     }
///
///     override pointerDown(event: PointerEvent): void {
///         let source = this.source;
///         if (source != null) {
///             Audio.play(source);
///         }
///         event.hit();
///     }
/// }
/// ```
export class AudioSource {

    /// The audio's own sample rate in Hz. Playback resamples it to the
    /// engine's rate, `Audio.sampleRate()`.
    get sampleRate(): u32;

    /// The number of audio channels.
    get channels(): u32;

    /// Releases the source now instead of when it is collected. Playing a
    /// released source returns null.
    release(): void;
}

/// What the audio thread drives. Extend `AudioProcessor` rather than this.
export abstract class AudioProcessorBase {
    /// Renders one block of `frames` interleaved frames into `out`, which
    /// arrives zeroed. `startFrame` is the block's first frame on the engine's
    /// clock, the one `Audio.timeFrame` reads. In a browser and on NRDP it
    /// counts the page's audio output instead, whose frames and rate
    /// `Audio.timeFrame` and `Audio.sampleRate` do not report. Runs on the
    /// audio thread, so it must neither wait nor allocate: drain rings with
    /// `receiveInto` and read snapshots with `latestInto`, into values made
    /// in init, rather than with `receive` and `latest`. A throw, a trap, or
    /// a block past the hard limit the host sets, 2 blocks by default, takes
    /// the processor out of the mix for good: its handle's `failed` says
    /// why, and only a new `Audio.start` plays again. In a browser and on
    /// NRDP a block past its hard limit ends at its next fuel check, which
    /// debug bakes and wasmFuel bakes give the processor; one without fuel
    /// ends only once it returns. A block that stalls the audio thread fails
    /// every processor: after a second in a browser, which drops the output,
    /// and after a tenth of a second on NRDP, which ends the thread.
    process(out: StaticArray<f32>, frames: i32, startFrame: f64): void;
}

/// Script that renders audio itself, started with `Audio.start`. It runs in
/// its own instance of the module, talking to other lanes only through the
/// shared memory in its argument: rings for messages and samples, snapshots
/// for knobs and meters, signals to wake a worker. A block reads them in place
/// with `receiveInto` and `latestInto`, which never allocate.
/// ```as
/// export class Knobs {
///     gain: f64 = 0.2;
///     pitch: f64 = 440;
/// }
///
/// export class Tone extends AudioProcessor<Snapshot<Knobs>> {
///     knobs: Snapshot<Knobs>? = null;
///     current: Knobs = new Knobs();
///     phase: f64 = 0;
///     rate: f64 = 0;
///     channels: i32 = 2;
///
///     override init(sampleRate: f64, maxFrames: i32, channels: i32, knobs: Snapshot<Knobs>): void {
///         this.knobs = knobs;
///         this.rate = sampleRate;
///         this.channels = channels;
///     }
///
///     override process(out: StaticArray<f32>, frames: i32, startFrame: f64): void {
///         this.knobs!.latestInto(this.current);
///         let channels = this.channels;
///         for (let i = 0; i < frames; i++) {
///             let sample = <f32>(Math.sin(this.phase) * this.current.gain);
///             for (let c = 0; c < channels; c++) {
///                 out[i * channels + c] = sample;
///             }
///             this.phase += 2 * Math.PI * this.current.pitch / this.rate;
///         }
///     }
/// }
/// ```
export abstract class AudioProcessor<A> extends AudioProcessorBase {
    /// Runs once before the first block: natively off the audio thread, in a
    /// browser on the audio worklet's render thread, so heavy setup there
    /// delays the mix. One still running after a second fails the processor,
    /// in a browser and on NRDP only when it has fuel. maxFrames is the most
    /// frames a block asks for, and channels how many interleave in each
    /// frame.
    init(sampleRate: f64, maxFrames: i32, channels: i32, arg: A): void;
}

/// A processor `Audio.start` started; `stop` takes it out of the mix.
export class AudioHandle extends Lane {
}

/// Plays `AudioSource` assets and reads the audio engine's clock.
///
/// Every play function returns the new `AudioSound`, or null when there is
/// no audio engine or the source was released.
/// ```as
/// let source = context.audio("myAudio");
/// if (source != null) {
///     // Start half a second from now.
///     let sound = Audio.playInTime(source, 0.5);
/// }
/// ```
export namespace Audio {
    /// Plays the source immediately.
    /// ```as
    /// let source = this.source;
    /// if (source != null) {
    ///     this.sound = Audio.play(source);
    /// }
    /// ```
    export function play(source: AudioSource): AudioSound?;

    /// Plays the source at an absolute engine time in seconds, to the
    /// millisecond, for scheduling against `Audio.time`.
    /// ```as
    /// let source = this.source;
    /// if (source != null) {
    ///     this.sound = Audio.playAtTime(source, Audio.time() + 1);
    /// }
    /// ```
    export function playAtTime(source: AudioSource, seconds: f64): AudioSound?;

    /// Plays the source after a delay in seconds, relative to the current
    /// engine time.
    /// ```as
    /// let source = this.source;
    /// if (source != null) {
    ///     this.sound = Audio.playInTime(source, this.scheduleSeconds);
    /// }
    /// ```
    export function playInTime(source: AudioSource, seconds: f64): AudioSound?;

    /// Plays the source at an absolute engine time in PCM frames, for precise
    /// scheduling against `Audio.timeFrame`.
    /// ```as
    /// let source = this.source;
    /// if (source != null) {
    ///     let frame = Audio.timeFrame() + Audio.sampleRate();
    ///     this.sound = Audio.playAtFrame(source, frame);
    /// }
    /// ```
    export function playAtFrame(source: AudioSource, frame: f64): AudioSound?;

    /// Plays the source after a delay in PCM frames, relative to the current
    /// engine time. Convert from seconds with frames = seconds *
    /// `Audio.sampleRate()`.
    /// ```as
    /// let source = this.source;
    /// if (source != null) {
    ///     this.sound = Audio.playInFrame(source, this.scheduleFrames);
    /// }
    /// ```
    export function playInFrame(source: AudioSource, frame: f64): AudioSound?;

    /// Returns the absolute time of the audio engine in seconds, a clock
    /// independent of any sound.
    /// ```as
    /// override advance(seconds: f64): bool {
    ///     this.engineTime = Audio.time();
    ///     this.engineTimeFrame = Audio.timeFrame();
    ///     this.sampleRate = Audio.sampleRate();
    ///     return true;
    /// }
    /// ```
    export function time(): f64;

    /// Returns the absolute time of the audio engine in PCM frames.
    export function timeFrame(): f64;

    /// Returns the sample rate of the audio engine in Hz. Use it to convert
    /// seconds to frames: frames = seconds * sample rate.
    export function sampleRate(): f64;

    /// Starts a processor rendering on the audio thread, mixed into the
    /// output, its argument deep copied into the processor's init. It returns
    /// at once: init runs later, natively off the audio thread and in a
    /// browser on the worklet's render thread, and the processor joins the
    /// mix at a block boundary. The factory names an exported processor
    /// class, which the processor's own instance constructs; the compiler
    /// writes each call, so Audio.start is never taken as a value.
    /// ```as
    /// this.player = Audio.start(() => new RingPlayer(), this.ring);
    /// ```
    @builtin export function start<A>(factory: () => AudioProcessor<A>, arg: A): AudioHandle;
}
